Overview
Our client is seeking an experienced Program Manager to lead the coordinated delivery of a large-scale, multi-year data center and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure program.
This individual will oversee the integrated program plan across design, engineering, construction, power, cooling, procurement, commissioning, and HPC infrastructure deployment. The role will connect facility delivery with compute, storage, networking, and platform readiness, ensuring all workstreams align with program milestones and operational requirements.
Individual Project Managers, engineering leaders, contractors, and functional teams will own specific scopes. The Program Manager will provide program-level oversight across schedule, budget, dependencies, risks, and delivery commitments, driving coordination from initial planning through operational turnover.
This hybrid position requires regular in-person collaboration in Dallas with executive leadership and engineering, construction, infrastructure, and operations teams.
Key Responsibilities
Program Delivery and Governance
Oversee end-to-end program delivery from planning and design through construction, infrastructure deployment, commissioning, and operational readiness.
Develop and maintain an integrated master program plan spanning facility development and HPC infrastructure workstreams.
Track program schedules, capital budgets, forecasts, milestones, quality, risks, and delivery performance.
Align individual project plans with overall program objectives, phased capacity requirements, and business commitments.
Establish consistent governance, reporting, milestone reviews, escalation processes, and accountability.
Maintain risk, assumption, issue, and dependency logs, along with change control and decision tracking.
Identify critical-path issues, resource constraints, and schedule conflicts; drive mitigation and recovery plans.

Data Center and HPC Infrastructure Integration
Coordinate dependencies across utility power, on-site generation, electrical distribution, cooling, controls, compute, storage, and networking.
Integrate HPC deployment milestones into the overall facility construction and commissioning schedule.
Align GPU and CPU hardware delivery, rack installation, high-speed network connectivity, storage deployment, and platform readiness with available power, cooling, and floor space.
Partner with technical leaders to track readiness for cluster installation, configuration, validation, and production handoff.
Coordinate high-density infrastructure requirements, including liquid cooling, rack power, network fabrics, and supporting mechanical systems.
Manage sequencing between facility turnover, equipment installation, infrastructure testing, and workload readiness.
Track dependencies across hardware vendors, infrastructure teams, platform engineering, and operations.

Cross-Functional and Project Coordination
Serve as the central coordination point across engineering, construction, procurement, supply chain, finance, technology, commissioning, and operations.
Provide program-level oversight across Project Managers responsible for individual projects, phases, and infrastructure workstreams.
Integrate project schedules and resolve issues that extend across multiple teams or scopes.
Align design completion, procurement, installation, testing, commissioning, and turnover activities.
Coordinate long-lead equipment, material availability, vendor capacity, and supply chain risks.
Partner with finance on capital planning, expenditure tracking, forecasting, and budget reporting.
Coordinate with utility providers, permitting authorities, municipalities, and other external stakeholders as required.

Vendor and Contractor Oversight
Monitor program commitments across general contractors, specialty contractors, engineering partners, equipment manufacturers, technology vendors, and commissioning providers.
Track performance against contractual milestones, schedules, quality requirements, and delivery expectations.
Identify vendor risks affecting construction progress, HPC deployment, commissioning, or operational readiness.
Ensure external partners understand program priorities, sequencing, and cross-functional dependencies.
Drive resolution of delivery gaps with internal workstream owners and external partners.

Schedule, Risk, and Change Management
Maintain visibility into the integrated master schedule and overall critical path.
Monitor procurement timelines, construction sequencing, infrastructure deployment, and commissioning dependencies.
Identify emerging risks and lead mitigation, contingency, and recovery planning.
Evaluate scope, design, and schedule changes for impacts on cost, capacity, technical readiness, and delivery milestones.
Ensure major changes are documented, approved, and communicated.
Escalate significant risks and decisions to senior leadership with clear business impacts and recommendations.

Commissioning and Operational Readiness
Integrate commissioning and technical validation activities into the overall delivery plan.
Coordinate construction completion, equipment startup, integrated systems testing, punch-list resolution, and turnover.
Track readiness across electrical, mechanical, controls, networking, security, life safety, and HPC infrastructure.
Partner with technical teams to incorporate cluster acceptance testing, performance validation, and infrastructure handoff into program milestones.
Ensure operations staffing, procedures, documentation, training, and support requirements are ready for turnover.
Support phased delivery where construction, commissioning, infrastructure deployment, and live operations occur simultaneously.

Executive Reporting
Maintain executive dashboards covering schedule, budget, procurement, construction, HPC deployment, commissioning, risk, and overall program health.
Provide clear visibility into critical-path activities, upcoming milestones, delivery forecasts, and required decisions.
Translate complex technical and construction issues into business impacts and actionable recommendations.
Maintain accurate forecasts for capital requirements, capacity availability, and operational turnover.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
10+ years of experience in program management, project management, data center delivery, infrastructure deployment, construction, engineering, or large-scale capital programs.
Demonstrated experience overseeing complex, multi-year, multi-phase infrastructure or construction programs.
Direct experience delivering data centers, HPC facilities, cloud infrastructure, colocation facilities, or comparable mission-critical technical environments.
Experience coordinating facility delivery with compute, storage, networking, or other technology infrastructure deployment.
Strong experience managing integrated schedules across multiple projects, contractors, disciplines, and workstreams.
Strong understanding of critical-path scheduling, dependency management, risk management, change control, forecasting, and program governance.
Experience coordinating engineering, construction, procurement, commissioning, and operational readiness.
Experience working with general contractors, engineering firms, equipment manufacturers, technology vendors, and commissioning providers.
Strong financial awareness and experience managing capital budgets and forecasts.
Proven ability to drive cross-functional issue resolution and communicate effectively with senior leadership.
Ability to work in a hybrid environment with regular in-person collaboration in Dallas.

Preferred Qualifications
PMP, PgMP, or comparable project/program management certification.
Experience delivering data center or mission-critical capital programs exceeding $250 million.
Experience supporting HPC, AI, GPU clusters, or other high-density compute environments.
Familiarity with HPC infrastructure, including GPU/CPU systems, high-speed Ethernet or InfiniBand fabrics, large-scale storage, and cluster platforms.
Familiarity with electrical distribution, generators, UPS systems, cooling plants, liquid cooling, controls, and commissioning.
Experience with utility coordination, electrical capacity development, permitting, and municipal stakeholders.
Experience coordinating hardware procurement, infrastructure installation, cluster validation, and production readiness.
Experience managing phased developments with concurrent construction, commissioning, technology deployment, and operations.

AI Fabrik builds an edge inference delivery network for high-performance tokens, with faster time-to-market from grid to tokens. Our mission is to build the inference infrastructure we wished every enterprise already had — close to users, close to the cloud, and extremely resilient for real-time workloads. AI Fabrik was incubated inside Gruve and backed by Mayfield , Xora (Temasek), Acclimate Ventures , Cisco Investments — existing investors from Gruve who followed us into this new chapter. We are deploying five initial production sites, with the first one coming online in July 2026.

About the Role

This role sits at the intersection of physical infrastructure deployment and software engineering. Our programs span the buildout of hardware sites across dozens of locations — facilities, power, networking, and compute — alongside the delivery of a deep software stack that must be production-ready when each site comes online.

The multiple related workstreams run in parallel and are tightly coupled. Hardware procurement and site construction operate on fixed schedules with limited room for adjustment. Software delivery must be planned and tracked with the same discipline. The TPM in this role is accountable for keeping both on track and ensuring the dependencies between them are managed proactively, not discovered late.

Key Responsibilities

Own the end-to-end planning and execution of large-scale technical programs: define scope, set milestones, sequence dependencies, and keep delivery on track across multiple engineering teams
Engage directly with system designs, architecture decisions, and infrastructure trade-offs — well enough to identify risks, ask the right questions, and flag issues before they compound
Manage cross-functional dependencies across engineering, product, design, data, and infrastructure; keep teams aligned without creating process overhead that slows them down
Communicate program status, risks, and decisions to different audiences — architectural context for engineering leads, delivery forecasts for product, business impact for executives — adapting the level of detail to what each stakeholder actually needs
Identify, track, and escalate technical risks early; own the mitigation plan and follow through to resolution rather than handing it off
Run the operational rhythm of the program: standups, steering meetings, decision logs, and retrospectives — with a bias toward async where possible
Write and maintain clear program documentation: specs, decision records, dependency maps, and status reports that teams actually read and reference
Drive post-launch reviews and feed learnings back into how the next program runs

Basic Qualifications

4+ years of experience in a technical role — software engineering, infrastructure, or a closely related discipline — before or alongside program management work
Demonstrable experience running large, cross-functional technical programs from planning through delivery
Comfortable reading system design documents, architecture diagrams, and API specs; able to engage meaningfully with engineers on technical trade-offs without needing to write the code
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adjust detail and framing depending on the audience
Experience managing dependencies and coordinating delivery across multiple teams simultaneously
Familiarity with project and program management tools (Jira, Confluence, Linear, or equivalent)
Solid understanding of modern software delivery practices: CI/CD pipelines, agile methodologies, and release management

Background in cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, or platform engineering — giving you the vocabulary and intuition to engage on architecture without needing a technical translator
Experience running programs in high-ambiguity environments where the scope evolves and the requirements are still being worked out
Familiarity with risk frameworks and structured approaches to dependency mapping across large engineering organizations
Experience coordinating security, compliance, or data privacy requirements as part of a technical program
Track record of improving how programs run — not just delivering on time, but leaving better processes behind

$160,000 - $240,000 USD + Benefits

Why AI Fabrik

At AI Fabrik, we hire for impact. We want those who challenge how inference infrastructure is built and who excel at delivering it in production. We are builders, architects, engineers, and researchers. We move fast, work with rigor, and care deeply about what runs in the real world.

The Rollout Program Manager (RPM)’s primary responsibility is to own the integrated rollout execution. This includes overseeing the launch plans, dependencies & milestone. The RPM will also help assess, identify and mitigate operational readiness, risk management, and escalations. The RPM will also coordinate functional deliverables and secure commitments from their owners.
The RPM sits within the Client Success Organization, reporting to the Chief Client Officer. The CCO and Client Success organization own ongoing client adoption, customer experience, and support. Within this context, the RPM coordinates rollout enablement and support readiness, monitors results, and drives follow-through with accountable owners. It may challenge readiness, recommend delaying or resequencing deployment, and escalate unresolved issues. Final decisions remain with designated functional and executive owners.

The RPM is NOT responsible for the following:
Product vision, strategy, roadmap, requirements, feature prioritization, product acceptance, and release scope remain with the Chief Product Officer and Product Management.
Positioning, messaging, differentiation, go-to-market strategy, and launch communications remain with Product Marketing under the CPO.
Engineering and AI leadership own technical delivery, quality, security, reliability, and technical readiness.

Working relationships

The RPM works closely with the CPO, Product Management, Chief AI Officer, Engineering, internal and outsourced development teams, Product Marketing, L&D, Client Success, support, participating coaches, and Firm module process owners.

Core responsibilities

Integrated rollout planning
Maintain one operating plan across platform modules and new services, with clear owners, milestones, dependencies, capacity needs, risks, and decisions. Coordinate initial launch phases and ongoing releases, using repeatable and automated workflows where practical.
Operational readiness and expansion
Translate approved product scope and service plans into readiness requirements for onboarding, training, communications, user participation, and support. Gather functional readiness evidence and present recommendations on deployment timing and expansion. Keep product release readiness distinct from operational rollout readiness.
Coach adoption and organizational change
Coordinate coach onboarding, training, office hours, and practical guidance for incorporating BIG Intelligence into coaching relationships. Develop early coach champions with L&D and Client Success, capture evidence of successful use, and identify resistance or workflow barriers that need action.
Client and Firm onboarding
Coordinate participant selection, rollout waves, access setup, onboarding, and feedback collection with the appropriate owners. Integrate platform onboarding into new coaching-client onboarding. Work with internal process owners to prepare Firm users for new capabilities and changes to their work.
Release enablement and communications
Coordinate Product Marketing, Product, and L&D deliverables so guidance, approved messaging, and training are ready when needed. Match enablement effort to the scale of the change and coordinate larger launches when appropriate.
Feedback and support coordination
Use Product’s established intake and classification process for defects and usability issues. Coordinate visibility and handoffs across product issues, training gaps, and adoption barriers without creating a parallel product backlog. Track unresolved issues and ensure clear ownership and user follow-through.
Scalable support readiness
Coordinate support workflows, knowledge resources, escalation paths, service expectations, and internal or third-party capacity. A designated internal software customer success/support owner manages support operations, vendor performance, and escalated case follow-through. Engineering and AI own technical diagnosis and fixes.
Measurement and continuous improvement
Maintain a concise scorecard covering readiness, activation, repeat use, coach participation, user feedback, support demand, and unresolved issues. Agree measures and targets with functional owners, compare rollout cohorts, and drive corrective actions. Transfer routine delivery tasks to operational owners while retaining responsibility for future rollout coordination and process improvement.

What success looks like

Launch phases and ongoing rollouts have clear owners, measurable readiness criteria, and credible plans. Leadership receives reliable evidence for deployment and expansion decisions.
Coaches, clients, and Firm users receive timely enablement and support; recurring rollout processes operate consistently and fit the release cadence.
Adoption and value measures inform action. Product owns product value and capabilities; Client Success owns ongoing client adoption and success; Firm process owners own internal business outcomes.

Required experience

At least five years in software program management, implementation, launch operations, or a closely related role, with direct accountability for delivery across multiple functions.
Taken at least two software products or substantial releases from a controlled pilot or Beta into broader customer availability, with concrete examples of personal ownership and results.
Managed rollout work beyond development delivery, including onboarding, training, communications, support readiness, and adoption.

Coordinated recurring SaaS releases and organizational change, including enablement and onboarding that continue after the initial launch.
Managed senior stakeholders and competing priorities, securing commitments and resolving dependencies without direct reporting authority.

new_jobs.title: Business Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
The Role

Pilot is building a first-of-its-kind, hybrid software/service solution to tackle the financial back office (bookkeeping, tax, CFO, etc.) so founders and business owners can focus on building and running their businesses. We work with thousands of customers in the tech startup and SMB sectors, and we're growing quickly.

Customer Operations is made up of 150+ employees who partner with our customers to manage their financial back office and support their business goals. This is an individual contributor role reporting into the Head of Business Operations, working closely with Customer Operations service delivery teams, cross-functional partners, and peer Business Operations Analysts.

This role sits at the center of how we plan, allocate, and forecast work across the organization, and increasingly, how we automate that work. Pilot is moving fast toward agentic, AI-assisted operations, and this person will build and own the systems, models, and reporting that make that shift possible: work orchestration, KPI reporting, resource forecasting, and billing. This isn't a role for someone who wants to build one dashboard and maintain it. It's for someone who wants to keep building better systems as the work itself changes.

The role requires real fluency with data and automation tools (Excel/Sheets at an expert level, plus a builder's instinct for where AI and scripts can replace manual work), sharp attention to detail, and good judgment about what results imply for our strategy and performance. This person works directly with senior leadership.

This is a hybrid in-office role based in our San Francisco office.

Key Responsibilities

Work Orchestration: Own the systems and processes that plan and allocate work across the organization. Build and maintain the models that route work efficiently as volume, team capacity, and service lines change.
KPI Reporting: Build and maintain reporting that gives leadership a clear, accurate, real-time view of business performance. Know the data well enough to catch anomalies before they become someone else's problem.
Resource Forecasting: Build and maintain forecasting models that project staffing and capacity needs against demand. Translate forecasts into recommendations leadership can act on.
Billing Operations: Own billing sheet accuracy and process, including the reconciliation and QA that keeps them error-free at scale.
Automation & AI Adoption: Identify where manual, spreadsheet-based, or repetitive work can be automated or AI-assisted. Build these solutions directly rather than just recommending them, using tools like Excel/Sheets scripting, SQL, and emerging AI tooling.
Process Optimization: Identify and implement improvements to the processes, workflows, and systems this role owns, so accuracy and efficiency improve as the business changes. When an improvement requires cross-functional buildout, lead it end to end, including the change management to get it adopted.

About You

Experience: 3-5 years in business operations, analytics, or finance, ideally in a start-up or technology-forward environment, with a track record of actually building and running a system. Experience owning forecasting, billing, or resource-planning is a strong plus.
Technical Proficiency: Expert-level Excel/Sheets (formulas, modeling, automation/scripting), plus working proficiency in SQL and analytics tools (e.g., Looker). Comfort using AI tools like Claude Cowork.
Detail Orientation: A track record of getting the numbers right the first time.
Systems Thinking: Able to see how planning, allocation, forecasting, and billing connect, and to design solutions that account for the whole picture rather than one piece of it.
Project Leadership: Demonstrated experience leading the build or overhaul of an operational system, including the change management needed to get a team to adopt it.
Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to work directly with senior leadership and translate technical or data-heavy work into clear recommendations.

About Pilot

Pilot launched in 2017 to bring the back office into the modern era. Pilot provides small businesses with dedicated finance experts - which Pilot hires as full-time, U.S.-based employees - who learn the ins-and-outs of their business. Pilot integrates directly with the billing, banking, expense, and payroll systems customers already use. With a special blend of custom software and expert bookkeepers, Pilot delivers accurate, consistent bookkeeping and financial management and tax services that give entrepreneurs the freedom to focus on their business.

Pilot has over 3,000 customers and has raised over $170 million in financing from Sequoia, Index Ventures, Stripe, Bezos Expeditions, and Whale Rock. Our investors also include a long list of world-class entrepreneurs, including Patrick and John Collison, Drew Houston, and Diane Greene. Our most recent funding round doubled our valuation to $1.2 billion – Meet Fintech’s Newest Unicorn.

Why Pilot?

We invest in our employees’ development and happiness because our employees are the keys to our success and ensuring happy customers
The opportunity to join a seasoned founding team that has led companies through two prior successful startups and acquisitions (by Oracle and Dropbox).
Flexible vacation/time-off policy
All federal holidays are observed

Coordinate projects from concept and protocol development through IRB review, implementation, analysis, dissemination, and closeout.
Epidemiologic and outcomes research: Lead or support analyses using electronic health records, cancer registries, administrative data, surveys, national surveillance datasets, and other complex sources. Apply appropriate methods, which may include survival analysis, multilevel modeling, causal inference, systematic review, meta-analysis, predictive modeling, and mixed or quantitative program-evaluation approaches.
Research operations and compliance: Maintain accurate protocols, regulatory files, data dictionaries, standard operating procedures, timelines, decision logs, and quality controls. Monitor milestones, research volume, workload, and deliverables; identify barriers early; and coordinate corrective action with investigators and institutional partners.
Grant and scholarly development: Contribute scientific methods, preliminary analyses, literature synthesis, budgets or resource assumptions, and project plans to grant proposals. Prepare and co-author abstracts, manuscripts, presentations, technical reports, and sponsor deliverables; support compliant post-award implementation and project closeout.
Team science: Collaborate with faculty investigators, clinicians, biostatisticians, trainees, community-engagement teams, research administrators, and external partners. Provide methodological consultation and mentor students or junior team members in study design, data analysis, reproducible workflows, and interpretation.

Tobacco Treatment Program —

Program leadership and daily operations: Manage the operational delivery and continuous improvement of TTS across the Cancer Service Line. Establish annual goals, workflows, referral pathways, service standards, outreach plans, performance measures, and reporting processes consistent with Cancer Service Line and Massey priorities.
Direct tobacco-treatment services: Plan and facilitate at least one structured group smoking-cessation session each week for patients, survivors, caregivers, or other approved participants. Provide evidence-informed education, behavioral counseling, relapse-prevention support, and connections to appropriate clinical and community resources within professional scope and institutional policy.
Care coordination and access: Partner with oncology, primary care, supportive services, pharmacy, nursing, social work, navigation, and digital-health teams to strengthen identification, referral, enrollment, follow-up, and continuity. Ensure timely documentation and escalation of medication, mental-health, safety, or other clinical issues to licensed treating professionals.
Institutional research collaboration: Build active collaborations with Massey and VCU tobacco researchers to integrate clinical service delivery with implementation science, population health, health-equity, and survivorship research. Support pilot studies, pragmatic evaluations, clinical research recruitment, and translation of evidence into practice.
Community engagement: Participate in community education, screening, outreach, and smoking-cessation activities, including partnerships serving populations with high tobacco burden or barriers to care. Adapt engagement strategies to community priorities and support bidirectional communication with community partners.
Research agenda and evaluation: Develop and maintain a multi-year TTS research and evaluation agenda aligned with Massey’s vision. Define priority questions, populations, outcomes, data sources, funding opportunities, dissemination plans, and partnership needs. Track reach, engagement, service delivery, treatment completion, patient-reported outcomes, quit-related outcomes, disparities, and implementation measures using approved definitions and methods.
Quality and sustainability: Use performance data, participant feedback, current evidence, and stakeholder input to improve service quality and access. Develop standard procedures, training materials, work aids, dashboards, and business cases that support responsible growth, funding, and sustainability.

Administration and Leadership —

Planning and reporting: Develop annual work plans, schedules, communication plans, metrics, and resource projections. Prepare concise reports and presentations for Cancer Service Line and Massey leadership, investigators, funders, and community partners.
Operational coordination: Facilitate meetings, clarify roles, coordinate assignments, and maintain productive relationships across participating units. Recommend process improvements and implement approved policy, workflow, or technology changes.
Training and functional leadership: Train staff, trainees, and collaborators in study procedures and tobacco-treatment workflows. Provide functional direction to assigned personnel; formal supervisory duties, if any, will follow the approved HR classification and organizational structure.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Doctoral degree in epidemiology, public health, population health, behavioral science, health services research, nursing science, a closely related discipline or an equivalent combination of training & experience.
At least three years of relevant research experience in cancer epidemiology, cancer survivorship, tobacco control, supportive oncology, population health, or a closely related area
Current Tobacco Treatment Specialist certification or documented ability to complete an approved certification within six months of appointment.
Demonstrated ability to design and implement research protocols, prepare IRB materials, manage study timelines and data, analyze results, and contribute to peer-reviewed dissemination.
Experience with quantitative epidemiologic methods and statistical programming using one or more platforms such as SAS, R, Stata, Python, SQL, SPSS, or an equivalent tool.
Experience working with one or more complex health-data sources, such as electronic health records, cancer registries, surveillance systems, administrative claims, clinical research data, surveys, or census-based datasets.
Demonstrated expertise or applied experience in tobacco cessation, tobacco-control research, behavioral intervention delivery, or implementation of evidence-informed health programs.
Ability and willingness to facilitate a minimum of one smoking-cessation group session each week, including occasional schedule flexibility needed to meet participant and community needs.
Strong scientific writing, presentation, group-facilitation, interpersonal, project-management, and time-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with investigators, clinicians, administrators, trainees, patients, and community partners and to foster an environment of respect, professionalism, and civility among people with varied backgrounds and experiences.
Research or program experience in an NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center, academic medical center, oncology practice, or cancer survivorship program.
Demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publications in cancer survivorship, tobacco cessation, cancer epidemiology, health disparities, supportive oncology, or related fields.
Experience conducting systematic reviews or meta-analyses and applying advanced methods such as causal inference, multilevel modeling, survival analysis, data mining, or predictive modeling.
Experience contributing methods, analysis plans, power calculations, or evaluation components to externally funded grants and community-engaged research initiatives.
Experience teaching, mentoring, or translating complex epidemiologic evidence for clinical, community, student, or executive audiences.
Demonstrated ability to work in and foster an environment of respect, professionalism and civility with a population of faculty, staff, and students from all backgrounds and experiences, or a commitment to do so as a staff member at VCU.

Preferred Qualifications

Clinical or health-professions training that supports effective collaboration with oncology care teams, while recognizing that this role does not independently practice outside the individual’s license or institutional privileges.
Experience developing dashboards or visualizations and implementing reproducible data-management and analytic workflows

About Tapestry

Tapestry is a group within Google working to build the AI-powered electric grid. We are tackling one of the world’s most important infrastructure challenges: helping the energy system become more visible, understandable, reliable, affordable, abundant, and clean.

Originally born at X, Alphabet’s moonshot factory, Tapestry brings together experts in energy, AI, software engineering, and products to build tools that help the electricity ecosystem plan smarter, move faster, and operate more efficiently.

This is a global effort. Tapestry supports partners across the U.S., U.K., Chile, New Zealand, Australia, and Brazil as they work toward a cleaner, more resilient energy future.

Joining Tapestry means doing high-impact work with a multidisciplinary team tackling a problem that matters at global scale. Learn more about our team and our mission here.

About The Role

Tapestry is looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive the execution and efficiency of how our Software Engineering, Product, Power System Experts, and cross functional teams work together in preparing our product development and commercialization.

This role will support the day-to-day progress of our software development, align both internal and external product priorities, and proactively identify and solve problems to guide the team through the dynamic phases of product development.. This is an incredibly dynamic role and requires high cross-functional communication, organization, and planning. They are accountable for the successful implementation of TPM processes, tracking progress against product and project goals, and driving velocity, efficiency, and teamwork without burning out stakeholders. You will work across AI, energy systems, and product teams to deliver foundational capabilities for the mission.

About The Team

IQVIA Institute for Human Data Science contributes to advancing human health by generating rigorous, evidence-based research. IQVIA Institute utilizes proprietary data sources, subject matter experts, advanced analytical skills, academic and external partners to conduct research and develop objective and data driven reports. These reports are intended for a broad set of stakeholders across the health system, such as policy makers, physicians, patients, societies, foundations etc. Our reports are widely downloaded with nearly 70,000 downloads last year along with over 600 citations in scholarly publications. Research at the IQVIA Institute can vary in size and complexity. We apply quantitative and qualitative analytical skills to a a variety of IQVIA data sources, external data sources and secondary literature to develop our reports. IQVIA Institute provides an opportunity to engage with crucial public health and public policy topics that can improve patient lives across the globe and to interact with key opinion leaders and stakeholders in these spaces. You'll enjoy a rewarding career in a collaborative, multicultural environment that values growth and development.

Role Overview

Project Managers are an integral part of funded research projects.

They are responsible for the on-time completion of projects or components of large, complex projects for clients in the life sciences field related to funded reports and research. They also identify and elevate potential new business opportunities and assists in the sales process. Their projects range in complexity from basic analysis and problem solving to assisting in the development of more complex solutions. PM's serve as project leaders and manage the client relationship associated with specific projects. These projects may be done in partnership with several other teams across IQVIA. The research and reports led by the senior consultant contribute to public health and public policy discourse across the globe and are well respected and used by stakeholders across the healthcare system (from policy makers, physicians, patients, societies, foundations etc.)

Participate or lead teams in the design, development and delivery of funded research projects or components of larger, complex projects.

Design, structure and deliver reports and presentations that are appropriate to the characteristics or needs of the audience.
Recommend improvements and alternative solutions to resolve problems.
Identify potential new business opportunities of follow-on work and new leads at assigned client.
Provide follow-up with client after project deliverable has been completed to ensure client satisfaction.
Proactively develop broader and deeper knowledge of methodologies and life sciences industry, healthcare policy globally through on the job experience and participation in training opportunities. Begin to develop subject matter expertise across healthcare system topics
When acting as Project Manager, proactively manage project timelines and manage day to day communication with the client and team members.

Bachelor's degree in life sciences, public health or other related field required. MBA, MPH, PhD with a life sciences or healthcare focus preferred.
Typically possesses 5-8 years of post-undergraduate experience or 3-5 years of post Masters experience.
Possesses solid project management skills and client management and relationship building skills.
Experienced with developing consultative relationships with senior level managers and executives at clients in the life science industry.
Ability to manage multiple projects, juggle priorities and deliver on tight deadlines.
Knowledge of consulting and research methodologies, tools and techniques related to functional area.

Necessary subject matter expertise to effectively manage projects.
Results oriented approach to work delivery and output. Ability to solve problems independently and creatively.
Effective communication - strong written and verbal communication skills including good command of English language. Excellent presentation, communication and client management skills.
Quality: High attention to detail and accuracy in work.

We’re looking for a curious and detail-oriented Data Analyst who enjoys working with data and turning it into meaningful insights. In this role, you’ll help us understand what the numbers are telling us, identify trends, and provide information that helps the team make better decisions.
You’ll work closely with different teams to understand their needs, solve business problems, and present findings in a clear and practical way. We’re looking for someone who is comfortable asking questions, enjoys solving problems, and can explain data in a way that makes sense to both technical and non-technical colleagues.
Key Responsibilities

Collect, clean, organize, and analyze data from different sources to ensure accuracy and reliability.
Work with business teams to understand their goals, challenges, and reporting needs.
Create and maintain dashboards, reports, and visualizations using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or Excel.
Use SQL to retrieve, manipulate, and analyze data from databases.
Identify patterns, trends, and potential issues that can help improve business performance.
Translate complex data into clear insights and practical recommendations.
Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and prepare regular reports for stakeholders.
Investigate data discrepancies and work with relevant teams to resolve them.
Support business planning and decision-making through data-driven analysis.
Look for opportunities to improve reporting processes, data quality, and analytical workflows.

Skills and Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Good working knowledge of SQL and data analysis techniques.
Experience with Excel and at least one data visualization tool, such as Power BI or Tableau.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an eye for detail.
Ability to interpret data, recognize trends, and explain findings clearly.
Good communication skills and the ability to work with people across different teams.
A willingness to learn new tools, ask questions, and explore better ways of working.
Ability to manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and maintain accuracy in day-to-day work.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means more than preparing reports. It means helping the team understand what is happening in the business and why. We value someone who is thoughtful, dependable, and genuinely interested in understanding data. You don’t need to have every answer right away, but you should be comfortable exploring problems, learning from feedback, and working with others to find the right answers.

If you enjoy connecting the dots, finding meaning in numbers, and helping people make better decisions, we’d love to hear from you.

new_jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You And The Role

Zipline is looking for a Technical Program Manager, Facilities to deliver the spaces and infrastructure that support our engineering, test, manufacturing, and workplace teams. You will lead facilities projects from initial requirements and feasibility through design, permitting, construction, commissioning, and operational handoff, with accountability for scope, budget, schedule, and readiness for use.

Working closely with Facilities, engineering stakeholders, EHS, IT, and external partners, you will translate evolving business needs into executable project plans. Your work will include new facilities, renovations, equipment installations, utility upgrades, and relocations, coordinating the building systems and operational dependencies required to bring each space into service.

We are looking for someone who combines technical judgment with hands-on program execution. You ask why a requirement exists, challenge assumptions with evidence, and find practical ways to meet competing needs. You can create clarity from incomplete information, hold partners accountable, and deliver projects in active environments where safety and operational continuity matter.

What You'll Do

Lead a portfolio of facilities capital projects, establishing scope, success criteria, budgets, schedules, and accountable owners from project initiation through handoff.
Partner with internal teams to define space, equipment, utility, and operational requirements. Separate essential needs from preferences and turn them into clear project scopes.
Coordinate architects, engineers, contractors, and specialty vendors through design, permitting, procurement, and construction. Set deliverables and resolve gaps between disciplines and project packages.
Use technical judgment to evaluate building-system capacity, equipment requirements, constructability, and maintainability. Challenge unnecessary scope and develop alternatives that improve cost or schedule while meeting safety and performance requirements.
Build integrated project schedules that account for permits, long-lead equipment, utility connections, shutdowns, and occupancy requirements. Identify critical dependencies and drive timely decisions.
Develop requests for proposals and evaluate bids with Procurement and project partners. Track commitments, forecasts, and change orders, and make clear recommendations on scope and spending decisions.
Coordinate site work, equipment installations, relocations, and shutdowns with Facilities, EHS, IT, and operating teams to protect safety and minimize disruption.
Maintain clear reporting on milestones, budgets, risks, and decisions. Escalate issues with a recommended path forward and drive recovery plans when delivery is at risk.
Lead readiness reviews and coordinate commissioning, inspections, punch-list completion, and handoff. Ensure Facilities and end users receive the documentation, training, and maintenance information needed to operate the space.

What You'll Bring

A track record of managing complex facilities, infrastructure, or construction programs from initial scope through operational handoff, with accountability for budget, schedule, and quality.
A technical foundation in mechanical, electrical, structural, architectural, or facilities engineering, construction management, or a related discipline, gained through education or equivalent practical experience.
Experience coordinating multidisciplinary consultants, contractors, vendors, and internal stakeholders, including work in active manufacturing, laboratory, R&D, or other technical environments.
The ability to read technical drawings, assess building-system and equipment dependencies, and ask the questions needed to identify design or execution risks. Working knowledge of permitting, construction sequencing, and commissioning.
Strong program management skills, including scope development, estimating, scheduling, bid evaluation, change management, and risk resolution across multiple concurrent projects.
Clear communication and sound judgment when priorities compete. The ability to explain technical trade-offs, recommend a path forward, and influence teams without direct authority.
A hands-on approach to execution, curiosity about how facilities support the business, and ownership of problems through resolution.

What Else You Need To Know

The starting cash range for this role is $160,000.00 - $205,000.00. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; overtime pay; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

new_jobs.description:
Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

The Facilities & Workplaces Project Specialist will be responsible for the planning, coordination, and delivery of capital projects across Roblox headquarters. This role will focus on managing office build-outs, renovations, infrastructure upgrades, reconfigurations, decommissions, and other capital improvements from initial planning through project closeout. This role will also complete commissioning, operational readiness, and the successful handoff of completed projects to the Facilities team responsible for the ongoing workplace experience and day-to-day operations.

This role will serve as a strategic partner and liaison amongst Facilities, Corporate Engineering, Security, Finance, Legal, business leaders, landlords, architects, consultants, contractors, vendors, and other project stakeholders.

This role is on-site at San Mateo HQ Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM.

You Will

Manage the complete lifecycle of assigned capital projects, including programming, scope development, design, budgeting, procurement, construction, commissioning, closeout, and operational handoff.
Support capital projects across Roblox headquarters and remote offices, including international locations.
Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, milestones, success metrics, and implementation plans.
Coordinate architects, engineers, consultants, general contractors, subcontractors, furniture vendors, technology partners, landlords, and internal stakeholders.
Lead project meetings and maintain clear documentation of decisions, responsibilities, risks, action items, and next steps.
Monitor project schedules, budgets, risks, change orders, and deliverables to ensure projects remain aligned with approved scope, cost, quality, and timing.
Review design drawings, specifications, construction documents, proposals, bids, and contracts for completeness and alignment with Roblox standards.
Coordinate with Procurement to develop bid packages, evaluate proposals, support vendor selection, and procure project-related services.
Review certificates of insurance for compliance and coordinate required documentation with vendors, landlords, Legal, and Risk.
Assist with annual capital planning, budget development, expenditure scheduling, forecasting, variance analysis, and corrective actions.
Support budget oversight by comparing actual project costs and commitments against approved budgets and forecasts.
Coordinate with Finance on purchase orders, invoices, accruals, forecasts, and project financial reporting.
Support contract management, invoicing, document control, change-order tracking, and project closeout documentation.
Serve as the primary liaison with Legal, Finance, Corporate Engineering, Human Resources, Global Security, Procurement, landlords, and other internal partners throughout the project lifecycle.
Coordinate construction access, security requirements, site logistics, shutdowns, inspections, testing, and work performed outside normal business hours.
Create and support communication plans aligned with project schedules, milestones, service interruptions, relocations, and completion dates.
Identify project risks, dependencies, and potential delays, and develop mitigation plans before they affect project delivery.
Develop project-specific success metrics and reporting to measure schedule, budget, quality, stakeholder satisfaction, and overall project performance.
Provide clear and consistent project updates to leadership, business partners, and affected employees.
Coordinate project-related furniture, fixtures, equipment, signage, technology, security, and workplace requirements.
Oversee project commissioning, punch-list completion, warranty documentation, training, asset information, and final acceptance.
Develop and maintain a formal project handoff process for the Facilities team, including operating manuals, warranties, as-built drawings, vendor contacts, preventive-maintenance requirements, training materials, and open-item tracking.
Partner with the Facilities team during the transition period to ensure completed spaces, equipment, amenities, and building systems are functional and ready to support employees.
Resolve project-related warranty, construction-defect, or incomplete-work issues before transferring full ownership to Facilities operations.
Provide limited post-occupancy support to confirm that completed projects meet operational and employee-experience expectations.
Provide general administrative and coordination support for project teams and local leadership, depending on project location.
Support the team as needed with capital projects, operational transitions, and other duties as assigned.

You Have

7–10+ years of experience managing corporate capital projects, workplace construction, office build-outs, renovations, or related facilities projects.
Demonstrated experience managing projects through the complete lifecycle, from initial planning and design through construction, commissioning, closeout, and operational handoff.
Strong knowledge of project scope, scheduling, budgeting, forecasting, procurement, contract administration, change management, risk management, and document control.
Ability to read and interpret architectural, engineering, design, and construction documents.
Experience coordinating architects, engineers, contractors, consultants, landlords, vendors, and cross-functional internal partners.
Strong cross-functional relationship building, collaborative problem-solving, teamwork, KPI implementation, project planning, program development, and project management skills.
Strong financial and analytical skills, including budget tracking, variance analysis, forecasting, invoice review, and change-order evaluation.
Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple capital projects and competing priorities simultaneously.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear project updates to stakeholders and leadership.
Ability to work independently, identify risks, make informed decisions, and drive projects through completion.
Availability outside normal business hours for scheduled projects, construction activities, shutdowns, relocations, and emergencies.

Workplace Strategy

Office Build-Outs, Renovations, Reconfigurations and Decommissions
Capital Planning
Budgeting and Forecasting

Agile Project Management
